newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber easier, fresh inquiries noted.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber easier, fresh inquiries noted.

text.p: Rubber futures ended lower on Tuesday with fresh inquiries from some foreign buyers helping to shore up prices in the local market, dealers said.
"There were some inquiries, but many of the sellers were not really keen about the low level of prices and very little was done as a result," a local rubber trader said.

Another dealer said: "There was some buying and shortcovering by some foreign outfits, but the tonnages done were very small and did not really have an impact in the market." Dealers said prices will probably continue to drift in the absence of sustained buying.
"Without any kind of buying impetus, the market really is neither here nor there. It will drift aimlessly," one dealer said.
At around 0945 GMT, November RSS3 was seen at 128.00-129.00 U.S. cents a kg from 129.25 cents.
November RSS1 was seen at 183.50-185.50 Singapore cents (US$1.30-$1.32) a kg from Monday's settlement of 185.50 cents.
November TSR20 was seen at 178.00-179.00 Singapore cents (US$1.26-$1.27) a kg from yesterday's 179.50 cents.
